chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥafṣ ibn al-Bakhtarī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام), who said:

Al-Anfāl are what no cavalry horse nor riding-beast was urged against, or a people who made peace, or a people who gave with their own hands, and every ruined land, and the interiors of the valleys. So it belongs to Rasūl Allāh (صلى الله عليه وآله), and it is for the Imam after him; he places it wherever he wills.

key_terms.أَعْطَوْا بِأَيْدِيهِمْ: they surrendered or handed over directly by their own hands
key_terms.الْأَنْفَالُ: non-military gains and designated properties placed under the authority of Rasūl Allāh (صلى الله عليه وآله) and the Imam
key_terms.بُطُونُ الْأَوْدِيَةِ: the inner parts or beds of the valleys
key_terms.بِخَيْلٍ: with cavalry horses used in warfare
key_terms.رِكَابٍ: riding-beasts or mounts used in expedition
key_terms.صَالَحُوا: they made peace or entered into a peaceful settlement
key_terms.يُوجَفْ: to be ridden or advanced swiftly in military mobilization

ai.seo_question: What is included in al-anfāl, and who has authority over it in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith defines categories of al-anfāl as properties and lands not acquired through actual military engagement, including lands surrendered peacefully and ruined lands. It states that such resources belong to Rasūl Allāh (صلى الله عليه وآله) and, after him, to the Imam, who has authority to dispose of them as he wills.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The Anfal is what has not been attacked upon by the cavalry horse nor expeditions, or (gained from) a people reconciled (by a peace treaty), or a people who give with their own hands, and every barren land and interior of the valleys, so it would be for Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, and it is for the Imam<sup>asws</sup> from after him<sup>saww</sup>. He<sup>asws</sup> would place it wherever he<sup>asws</sup> so desires to’.
en.sarwar: 2. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from Aban from Muhammad ibn Muslim from abu Ja‘far (a.s.) who has said the following. about the words of Allah, the Most High. “Know that whatever property you may gain, one fifth belongs to God, the Messenger, the kindred,. .” [8:41]
The Imam (a.s.) said, “It refers to the relatives of the Messenger of Allah. Al-Khums (one fifth) belongs to Allah, the Messenger and to us.”
